content:
maria: Heads up — a user hit a weird typing/runtime combo: our JS SDK builds fine in Node but crashes on Vercel Edge with `TypeError: require is not defined`. They also got TS errors about overloads and generics when upgrading to v2 of the SDK. :thinking:
jonathan: Hmm, is their project ESM-only? Edge runtimes are strict about that. What does their package.json and tsconfig look like?
maria: package.json has "type": "module" and tsconfig uses "module": "ESNext", "target": "ES2020". But they import the CJS entry with `const { Redwood } = require('redwood-inference')` in some sample.
priya: Classic mismatch. If package is ESM, require will blow up on edge. We should ensure our SDK ships a proper ESM entry and also an export for CJS or document how to import.
samir: On the typing side they opened an issue: our `createClient` overloads look like `createClient(opts: ClientOptions): Client` and `createClient<T extends Model = Model>(opts: ClientOptions & { model: T }): Client<T>`. Their TS complains about inference and ends up with `any` or `unknown` in generics.
jonathan: Can you paste the exact error?
maria: From their repo: `TS2345: Argument of type '{ apiKey?: string | undefined; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'ClientOptions & { model: T; }'.` They removed explicit model field because defaults should infer it.
priya: We probably need a fallback overload `createClient(opts?: ClientOptions): Client<Model>` so callers who omit model still get a typed client. Also we should avoid overly strict generic constraints that force them to provide `unknown` vs `any`.
samir: Also they flagged `unknown` in responses: our response type is `Response<unknown>` and their IDE suggests `any` for convenience. We should provide helper `parseResponse<T>()` or make top-level generics simpler: `Client<T = any>` with strict alternative `Client<Parsed>` for advanced users.
jonathan: For edge compatibility we should mention bundler flags and tsconfig: recommended tsconfig snippet ->
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true
  }
}
```
And package.json: "type": "module", "exports": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"}
maria: Good call. The user is also hitting runtime because their bundler (esbuild via Vercel) inlines something that expects `globalThis.process`. Edge workers don't have process. We need to ensure our runtime uses `globalThis` safe guards and avoids `process.env` checks at module top-level.
priya: Action items: 1) Add an overload `createClient(opts?: ClientOptions): Client` that maps to a default model generic. 2) Provide a README snippet for ESM/CJS and edge bundlers. 3) Offer a small sample app for Vercel Edge with minimal tsconfig + package.json that we can link in onboarding.
jonathan: For typings change I'd propose: keep `unknown` in internal libs but export types with helpful aliases, e.g. `type SDKResponse<T = any> = ResponseShape<T>` and `function parseResponse<T = any>(res: SDKResponse<T>): T` so consumers can opt-in. That avoids forcing `unknown` on everyone.
samir: Also warn about top-level require/use of `fs` or conditional imports. We should add a lint rule to sample apps to fail fast if CJS-only patterns used.
maria: I'll draft a tiny repro and a suggested PR that adds the overloads + README guide. Will ping once ready. @devex-bot can you create a tracking GH issue for "sdk: improve ts overloads + edge guide"? :eyes:
devex-bot: Created issue #3214: "sdk: improve ts overloads + edge guide" and linked this thread.
priya: Nice. Once PR is up we can add a line to the migration guide about `unknown` -> `any` tradeoffs and the recommended `Client<T = any>` ergonomic default.
jonathan: Great — thanks team. If anyone sees other Edge+TS crash patterns (e.g., `Buffer` polyfills, `process.cwd()` usage), drop them in this thread.
maria: Will do. Shipping the PR draft by EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
